title: feat: rule checks and tracking cuts
headline: Four of the owner's standing rules are now held by checks instead of prose, the dash-name wildcard check reads a command as bash splits it, release text is written from the build record and checked against it, and the list shows open rows with an archive beside it.
alignment: v1.46.0 is build 20 of the v2.0 plan: K150 to K153, K155, K156, E18, TC0 to TC3, part of TC5 and the release-format fix, each reproduced on the released 1.45.0 or proven by a run first.

items.text: A local test run reaches only the test files the branch changed; a run of the whole suite, `test-run.mjs --changed`, an unchanged test file or a check that is the CI's job waits for the owner's pop-up yes.
items.where: Running the whole suite locally on a feature branch
items.test: tests/guard-dispatch.test.mjs::a local test run reaches only the tests the branch changed; the rest waits for the owner

items.text: The kit's test runner refuses a full or `--changed` run off CI unless given `--owner-yes`; a named file, `--pick` and `--map` run as before.

The sweep meter answers with the call cap and token ceiling before any other reviewer hold; build 19's role 1 ran to 1,072,274 tokens against 749,524 because a shell refusal answered first, six times.
A meter that cannot read a reviewer's transcript lets the call through and writes the cause to the git folder's log; the sweep outcome then keeps auto-approval paused and names the role.
The test check names each new test the build record does not name, and a medium or low sweep fix that adds a new test instead of a row in an existing one, unless the fix gives a reason.
A working-memory line that keeps rule wording the kit has retired fails the state check the closeout runs, and session start names it; a line marked (history) is skipped.
items.where: A stale rule note left in the working memory
items.before: Read and acted on by later threads
items.after: Fails the closeout until it goes
items.test: tests/state.test.mjs::a working-memory line that keeps retired rule wording fails the check, unless marked as history

items.text: The dash-name wildcard check reads a command as bash splits it (quotes, `$?`, here-documents), reads only a wildcard in the first path part, in each folder a cd reaches; what it cannot follow gets its own reason.
items.where: A read such as ls with a wildcard in a folder part, or echo exit=$?

items.text: A choice pop-up that names an item code with too few plain words beside it, or asks to approve a plan with no Overview, is sent back to be rewritten before the owner sees it; the plan format opens with that Overview.
items.test: tests/guard-dispatch.test.mjs::a choice pop-up that offers item codes with no plain words, or a plan with no overview, goes back to Claude

items.text: `build-record.mjs release` writes the release notes file and prints the one publish line with its title, and the release check compares the live title and notes with the record.
A Feature, First push or Launch gate review must name Privacy, Supply chain, Legal, Code security and a gaps or test value row, in the build record and in the PR body audit.
A list row is marked done only with a verify file in the project that holds the release check's RELEASE COMPLETE line for its release; closed rows need none.
The list's rows view shows open rows only; done and closed rows go to a new archive view written from the same data, so each row appears in exactly one of them.
items.where: The rows block a thread reads at start
items.after: Open rows; the rest in the archive block

items.text: `state.mjs board <page.html>` writes the status board from the list data: one page, one column per tag, one card per row.
items.test: tests/list.test.mjs::board writes one self-contained page from the list data, every row one card in its tag column

items.text: The Working Memory template points at the generated phase line and the decision record instead of keeping its own Phase Status and Locked Architectural Decisions sections.

verification: Each guard row was reproduced on a throwaway clone of the released 1.45.0 first; the meter cause came from replaying build 19's role 1 transcript call by call.
A start-up run from the short list view picked the same next item, scope and tools as one from the full list, at $0.35 against $0.70.
Each changed test was run red on the code before it and green after.

decisions.decision: Rule prose copies are cut outside the kit text
decisions.why: The kit's rule files hold almost no copy of these four rules; they live in memory and briefs, so no kit rule line changes and no recall run is needed.

decisions.decision: The Session Log stays in the start order for now
decisions.why: Moving it changes the start file's read order, which needs a recall run; it rides with K118 in the next build that pays for one.

decisions.decision: Quoted inline code and here-document bodies stay held by the write reading
decisions.why: They fail safe and are the named limit K154; the dash check itself now reads them as bash does.
New checks reach every project: local test runs, pop-ups, the list views, done rows and the PR audit.

decisions.decision: The release check's log binds a version, not a repo
decisions.why: The workbench checks the kit's releases by design, so its origin is never the checked repo; the log sits in the project's own .git folder, which no tool writes.

upgrading: Run install user, then install project. The next render adds an archive block after the rows block where a project has none, so done and closed rows stay in sight. Marking a row done for a release now needs `item set <id> verify <result file>`, a file holding the release check's RELEASE COMPLETE line, and that check run in the project, which logs it in the project's .git folder.
limits: The test-scope check reads the common runners (node, npm, pnpm, yarn, bun, jest, mocha, pytest, go, cargo, dotnet and the like) by name; one it does not list is not read. The pop-up check reads choice pop-ups and plan files only; a chat message is not checked. The retired-wording check reads the patterns it lists, not the same rule in other words. A done row whose release names no version (a project that ships none) needs only its verify file. The release check log is read only in a main checkout, not a worktree.
